newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS SUFFERS FIRST LOSS OF 1997 AT INDIAN WELLS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS SUFFERS FIRST LOSS OF 1997 AT INDIAN WELLS.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras suffered his first loss of the year Wednesday when 43rd-ranked Czech Bohdan Ulihrach beat him 7-6 (7-5) 7-5 in the second round of the Champions Cup.
Sampras arrived on stadium court having won all 17 matches he played in 1997 and with an overall 20-match winning streak. He also had won 34 consecutive hardcourt matches, dating back to August 1996.
With the premature departure of several stars, the tournament could become a splendid opportunity for players normally relegated to an understudy role.
In addition to Sampras, the curtain came down Wednesday on fourth seed Goran Ivanisevic of Croatia, sixth seed Thomas Enqvist of Sweden and 15th seed Alex Corretja of Spain.
Heading into just the third round of action, the 16 seeds have been diminished to five.

In the top half, only 14th seed Alberto Berasategui of Spain remains. Seeds still remaining in the bottom half are second seed Thomas Muster of Austria, third seed and defending champion Michael Chang, eighth seed Carlos Moya of Spain and 13th seed Marc Rosset of Switzerland.

Before the shock of Sampras's losing could even sink in, the fifth-ranked Ivanisevic became the next stadium court victim as 53rd-ranked wildcard American Jonathan Stark needed only 65 minutes to outplay the Croatian 7-5 6-3.
"Today on the court, I didn't feel it," Ivanisevic said. "I wasn't pumped."
On an outside court, 55th-ranked Chris Woodruff, a semifinalist last week in Scottsdale, upset eighth-ranked Enqvist 6-4 6-4.
A hand injury forced the 22nd-ranked Corretja from the competition with 59th-ranked Slava Dosedel of Czech Republic leading 6-4 4-1.
Both Sampras and Ulihrach analysed their one hour, 28 minute match as less a case of the Czech playing well than the American playing subpar. And that left Sampras totally frustrated.
"I really didn't perform at my best, nowhere near it," Sampras admitted. "It's tough to accept when you don't play the way you want to play. I can only beat myself up so much by talking about it."
Ulihrach was pleased to win his second victory in three matches against Sampras.
"You can imagine how nice it is to beat him because he won 20 matches in a row," Ulihrach said. "It's an unbelievable feeling. I didn't expect to win today."
Sampras, a former two-time champion here, had three set points in the 12th game, but there was never to be any service breaks in the first set.
On Sampras's serve on the final point of the tiebreaker, Ulihrach benefitted when he hit a forehand from the baseline that nicked the net and tumbled over onto Sampras's side.

The players traded service breaks in the opening two games of the second set and stayed on serve until the last game. Serving at 30-30 in the 12th game, Sampras netted a forehand half volley and then fell victim to a screeching forehand crosscourt passing shot on the final point.
